posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
It seems like a good power, but I can see some drawbacks.

If both cards are not helpful (or outright hurtful, like inventory barrage/self sacrifice/know when to turn loose) you HAVE to play one of them.  its not optional.  more often than not, its going to be useful- but it could bite you.  Another potential area is that the base power has no ways of activating his songs, which makes him MUCH more reliant on his instruments.  So he's going to be a bit more of a slow burn in order to get those wonderful combos, and he has even less HP to get things going.

OX is a lot sturdier than the adept, and has a lot more ways to do things automatically (IE: start of turn) that aren't dependant on his power.  so he can get a LOT of stuff done and still use his base power to help the group (or further his own setup).  This version of the Adept would have a much quicker start (in that he can start letting other people do stuff) right away, but sacrifices some of his long term flexibility to do it.

Inside of his own deck I love the base power.

Inventive preparation and his base power?  Awesome.

Vernal Sonata and his Base Power?  Awesome.

My negative reaction comes from Omnitron-X's power being so cheesy powerful vs. certain villains and situations, and now Adept gets to do that and put a hero card in play at the same time.

I'd just prefer it were limited to hero decks.

I've always hated power creep, and sometimes I think I am seeing it in this game.

Mostly I'm wrong, I hope I continue to be.
